data.name: Random Access Murder
data.detailed_description:
Upcoming features

Over the coming weeks we will add character progression and customization, stay tuned!


Acerca do jogo

You're a robot. Murder other robots with your data-destroying weapons and create a stack of dismantled enemies. Be the last heap standing and DO NOT RUN OUT OF MEMORY! RAM is a 1st person arena shooter with a unique look and fast-paced action. Play online against your friends (or enemies) across 5 arenas. The 9 different weapons in the game won't hurt your opponents, but rather leak their memory, causing different glitches and bugs.

reviews.review:
Random Access Murder is a Humble Monthly cash-in that should have been made to be a Humble Original rather than a featured game in the bundle it was included in. It's a very generic FPS that relies on a "tron" aesthetic, with very little features and not much to set it apart from other games in the same genre. 

The one unique feature this game has is its use of "glitches" that occur when you're damaged by other players, which include blue screen errors, pop-ups, crashes to desktop, and other similar visual effects which are designed to mimic old Windows hardware errors or signs of a virus/malware infected machine. This is pretty much the only cool aspect about the game and it can be more of a frustration the longer you play the game as it tends to get in the way of the gameplay. These effects tend to hide how crappy the shooting mechanics are rather than help the aesthetics in the long term.

There's very little gun and level variety, and the guns tend to be very unreliable for the most part. The most efficient gun to me seems to be the Rocket Launcher, which has more of a direct impact than every other gun. There's also a grenade launcher (that has a flash effect) which is interesting at first, but quickly gets tiresome when you realize it doesn't have much of a damage effect. Other guns are a bit ambiguous as to what effects they have, which can be a fatal flaw for a shooting game. There are currently 4 levels included in the game which are uninspired. The game could benefit from workshop support, I doubt it'd be very complicated to design your own levels.

As far as the interface goes, there are barely any options you can customize, and there are basic features that seem to be missing like a scoreboard or the ability to edit control bindings. Someone please correct me if I'm wrong, because if there is a way to access the score list, I haven't seen any. There's no way to check for control bindings in game, you just have to assume what the default controls are. I'm also not sure if the server names are currently working, every server I see pop up has a generic number which is indistinguishable from the rest. I've had no issues connecting to games at least, so the game does have competent netcode working for it.

The dev claims that eventually character progression and customization will be added, but in the current state I can't recommend this game at ANY price. There are better shooters that you can play for free, and if you need something with a retro "tron" art style, then I suggest playing Robot Roller Derby Disco Dodgeball. It's not an FPS but it's leagues better than this game.
